description:

title: Agent terminal gets stuck on interactive package manager prompts (needrestart, debconf, pipe buffering)
description:
## Summary

The agent terminal tool fails to handle two classes of interactive prompts, causing consistent eval failures on terminalbench2 tasks that copilot-cli passes.

## Problem 1: needrestart/debconf TUI prompts

When `apt-get install` triggers needrestart, a "Which services should be restarted?" TUI prompt appears. None of the `detectsHighConfidenceInputPattern()` or `detectsLikelyInputRequiredPattern()` patterns in `outputMonitor.ts` match this format. The `idleSilence` timer fires after 60s, the tool returns "moved to background", and the agent gives up.

**Example**: `nginx-request-logging` — agent ran `apt-get install -y nginx`, needrestart prompted, agent waited 5 minutes then sent an empty `send_to_terminal` and stopped. copilot-cli finished the same task in 33 seconds.

## Problem 2: Pipe buffering hides prompts

When the model pipes an interactive command through `tail`/`head`/`grep`, the pipe buffers all output until the upstream closes. Interactive prompts (like opam `[Y/n]`) never reach the terminal buffer, so the `OutputMonitor` cannot detect them.

**Example**: `compile-compcert` — agent ran `opam install coq -y 2>&1 | tail -20`. The opam depext `[Y/n]` prompt was buffered by `tail` and never visible to the output monitor. The `[Y/n]` pattern *would* match `detectsHighConfidenceInputPattern` if it reached the terminal — the bug is the pipe hiding it.

## Fix

1. Set `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` in the copilot agent terminal env vars (in `toolTerminalCreator.ts`), alongside existing `GIT_PAGER`, `GIT_EDITOR`, etc. This prevents apt/dpkg from ever opening interactive prompts.

2. Add system prompt guidance telling the model to never pipe interactive commands through filters.

## Impact

Found via terminalbench2 eval analysis comparing vscode-copilot-cli vs copilot-cli. These two issues account for 2 of 12 consistent regressions (~13% score gap).

title: Agent host: client tool calls in the default chat hang (never resolved)
description:
## Problem

Client-provided tool calls running in a session's **default chat** can hang: the SDK handler's deferred is never resolved, so the agent waits forever on a tool result that already came back.

## Root cause

`ChatToolCallComplete` envelopes are emitted on the chat channel URI, which is formatted as:

```
ahp-chat://<chatId>/<base64(sessionUri)>
```

In `agentSideEffects.ts`, both dispatch paths forwarded that chat URI straight into `IAgent.onClientToolCallComplete(session, ...)`. But every agent keys its `_sessions` map by the raw session id, resolved via `AgentSession.id(uri)` = `uri.path.substring(1)`. For a chat URI that path is the **base64 blob**, not the session GUID, so the default-chat lookup never matched and the completion was silently dropped.

This affected the copilot, claude, and codex agents. Peer (additional, non-default) chats happened to still work because they resolve through a separate `_chatSessions` map keyed by the chat URI.

## Fix

Forward the resolved session URI for the default chat (so `AgentSession.id` yields the GUID), and keep forwarding the chat URI for peer chats. Tracked in [#323302](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/323302).

## Follow-ups to consider

- The footgun is that `onClientToolCallComplete(session, ...)` accepts a URI that is sometimes a session URI and sometimes a chat URI, and each agent re-derives routing. Worth considering a clearer contract or a single shared resolution helper so this can't silently regress.
- Add broader coverage that the URI handed to agents at the side-effects boundary is always the one the agent can resolve.

title: Copilot session restore splits one interaction into multiple chat responses
description:
## Type of Bug

Bug

## Description

Restoring an Agent Host Copilot session can split one SDK interaction into multiple AHP turns and therefore multiple `ChatResponseViewModel` instances. The additional requests have empty prompts.

The Copilot SDK can persist empty `assistant.message` events with no tool requests immediately before another assistant message in the same `interactionId` and SDK `turnId`. The live adapter ignores these non-renderable messages, but `mapSessionEvents` treats every parent assistant message without tool requests as the end of the current turn. The following assistant message then has no active builder, so history replay creates a fallback turn with an empty user message.

The resulting chain is:

1. `mapSessionEvents` prematurely finalizes the parent turn.
2. The next assistant message creates a fallback turn with an empty prompt.
3. `turnsToHistory` emits a request/response pair for every reconstructed turn.
4. `ChatServiceImpl` and `ChatViewModel` create multiple top-level response view models.

Captured restored models showed six empty requests created within the same millisecond. Their request IDs exactly matched the orphaned SDK `assistant.message` event IDs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a tool-heavy Copilot Agent Host conversation that produces multiple SDK model rounds.
2. Switch away from the session or restart/reopen it so history is rebuilt from SDK events.
3. Inspect the chat model or rendered transcript.
4. Observe multiple requests/responses with empty prompts for what was one live interaction.

## Expected Behavior

All assistant messages belonging to the same SDK interaction are reconstructed into one AHP turn and one top-level chat response, preserving markdown/tool ordering. Empty, non-renderable assistant events must not create a turn boundary.

## Relevant Code

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/mapSessionEvents.ts`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mapSessionEvents.test.ts`

(Written by Copilot)

title: Copilot Chat auto-switches to 1M context after VS Code restart, ignoring selected model setting
description:
* Copilot Chat Extension Version: latest
* VS Code Version: latest
* OS Version: latest
* Feature: Copilot Chat / existing chat session after VS Code restart
* Selected model: GPT 5.5 High 272k

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set Copilot Chat to use GPT 5.5 High with 272k context.
2. Start or continue a Copilot Chat session.
3. Restart VS Code.
4. Continue the existing Copilot Chat session.
5. Check the model/context shown in the Copilot UI.

## Expected Behavior

Copilot should respect the currently selected model/context setting after VS Code restart.

If I selected GPT 5.5 High 272k, continuing an existing session should keep using GPT 5.5 High 272k, unless I explicitly choose another model/context.

## Actual Behavior

After restarting VS Code and continuing an existing session, Copilot appears to ignore the selected setting and silently switches to the 1M context option.

This is especially serious because 1M is much more expensive. The switch is not explicitly confirmed by the user, but the user is still charged for the more expensive option.

## Impact

This caused unexpected billing charges for me. In one case, I paid around $10 because Copilot silently switched to the 1M option.

This makes Copilot unsafe to use with paid models/context tiers, because the UI setting is not reliably respected across VS Code restarts.

## Request

Please investigate why continuing an existing session after VS Code restart can override the user-selected model/context setting.

At minimum, Copilot should never silently switch to a more expensive model/context tier without explicit user confirmation.

title: Feature request: Display cache_write_price in the Cost column of the Models management UI
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

The **Cost (Credits per 1M Tokens)** column in the Models management UI currently displays **Input**, **Cache** (read), and **Output** costs. However, the CAPI `token_prices` response also includes a `cache_write_price` field that is not surfaced anywhere in the UI.

**Example CAPI response fragment:**

```json
"token_prices": {
    "batch_size": 1000000,
    "default": {
        "cache_price": 50,
        "cache_write_price": 625,
        "context_max": 200000,
        "input_price": 500,
        "output_price": 2500
    },
    "long_context": {
        "cache_price": 50,
        "cache_write_price": 625,
        "context_max": 936000,
        "input_price": 500,
        "output_price": 2500
    }
}
```

**Requested feature:**

Add a **"Cache write"** entry alongside the existing cost items (In, Cache, Out) in the Cost column so that users can see the full per-model pricing breakdown directly in the UI.

- Show `cache_write_price` (and its long-context variant) from the CAPI response in the same format as the other cost fields (e.g. "Cache write: 625").
- Include it in hover tooltips (e.g. "Cache write: 625 credits per 1M tokens").
- When the value is missing or null, display a consistent fallback matching the behavior for other absent costs.
- Support both default and long-context pricing rows in the model picker hover table.

**Why this matters:**

Cache write cost can be significantly higher than cache read cost (e.g. 625 vs 50 credits). Without this information in the UI, users cannot fully evaluate model pricing and may underestimate actual usage costs. The data is already returned by the API — it just needs to be displayed.

Run in terminal tool returns 'Failed to retrieve command output' when output exceeds scrollback
description:
## Problem

When a command's output exceeds the terminal's scrollback buffer (`terminal.integrated.scrollback`, default 1000 lines), the `run_in_terminal` tool returns "Failed to retrieve command output" instead of returning whatever is available in the buffer.

## Expected behavior

The tool should return the full scrollback buffer contents (i.e. the last N lines that fit in scrollback) rather than failing entirely. Even partial output is more useful than an error message.

## Repro

1. Set `terminal.integrated.scrollback` to a low value (e.g. 100)
2. Have the agent run a command that produces more lines than the scrollback (e.g. `seq 1 5000`)
3. Tool result says "Failed to retrieve command output"

## Notes

This is separate from the large output truncation/file-write handling in #321640 — that PR handles the case where output is successfully retrieved but exceeds the inline size limit. This issue is about output never being retrieved at all.

Users with color deficiencies cannot distinguish inline links from surrounding body text. They may miss important navigation options entirely. 

## Repro Steps 
Open VS Code > Copilot chat > Permission Picker combo box > Bypass approvals > “chat.permissions.default" link > Observe the issue: Links distinguished only by color 

## Actual Result 
The link “chat.permissions.default” is visually distinguished only by color (blue text) and does not have any additional non-color visual indicator such as underline or styling.

## Expected Result 
Links should have a non-color visual indicator (e.g., underline, bold text, or icon) in addition to color so that they are distinguishable from surrounding text for all users.

## How to Fix 
Add text-decoration: underline to inline links, or provide another non-color visual cue (bold, border-bottom). Ensure the link color also meets 3:1 contrast against surrounding text.

Application Name: VS Code 
VS Code version: 1.124.2
